title: Ephemeral burst shielding: SLA matrix and tenant burn-control playbook
creator: Marcus V. Reyes
description:
Problem: Hosted API customers occasionally create short-lived traffic spikes (scheduled batch jobs, repeated curl loops, or misconfigured clients) that blow through aggregated capacity and degrade tail latency for interactive tenants. Current global circuit breakers are too coarse: they either let a noisy tenant consume headroom or throttle everyone.

Goal: Define an SLA/SLO matrix and operational playbook that: 1) specifies latency and availability targets for interactive vs batch/async workload classes, 2) allocates ephemeral burst allowances per tenant and provides burn-controls with graded mitigation, and 3) defines rollout gates and monitoring alerts for any changes to burst policy. The outcome must be actionable for runtime, routing, and console teams (SRE and Engineering) to implement policy enforcement and for customer-facing teams to explain the behavior to customers.

Scope: Hosted API (public endpoints) initially; design must be extensible to Dedicated and Private. Focus areas: measurement windows, per-tenant burst budgets, backpressure thresholds, canary gating for policy changes, alerting/ownership, and acceptance criteria for PRD sign-off.

Out of scope: Deep datastore quotas, per-model fine-grained QPS shaping, and billing changes (billing will be addressed in follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Define clear SLOs for interactive endpoints: p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 750ms for 'standard' tenant class under nominal load (window = 5m)
Define separate envelope for batch/async endpoints: p50 <= 300ms, p95 <= 2s, availability >= 99.5% (window = 1h)
Specify per-tenant ephemeral burst budget (tokens/minute) and an observable burn-rate metric surfaced in Console and Grafana

Design three-tier mitigation actions triggered by burn-rate and sustained tail degradation: soft-throttle (priority queuing), hard-throttle (rate limit), and graceful degrade (route to fallback model). Each action must have a defined SLA impact and automatic rollback timer

Establish canary rollout plan for policy changes: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with success criteria (no >20% relative increase in tenant p99 or increase in platform error budget burn) and automated abort on threshold breaches
Create alerting rules and runbooks: burn-rate alert, cross-tenant-tail alert, and runaway-tenant alert with clear on-call playbooks and escalation path
Provide a signed-off PRD and a Console mock showing per-tenant burst budget and historical burn visualization
Implement end-to-end contract test that simulates 100x ephemeral bursts from a tenant and verifies mitigation actions occur and restore tail latency within 10 minutes
